q: What is the fastest land animal in the world?
fact: Cheetahs can sprint up to about 60 mph in short bursts to catch prey.

q: What is the largest land animal in the world?
fact: African elephants can weigh more than 6 tons and stand over 3 meters tall at the shoulder.

q: What is the tallest land animal in the world?
fact: A giraffe's heart weighs about 11 kilograms to pump blood all the way up its long neck.

q: Which animal is famous for its black and white stripes?
fact: No two zebras have exactly the same stripe pattern, each one is unique.

q: Which flightless bird lives in Antarctica and is an excellent swimmer?
fact: Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 meters in search of food.

q: What do giant pandas eat almost all of the time?
fact: Giant pandas spend 10 to 16 hours a day eating bamboo.

q: Which animal hops on powerful hind legs and carries its baby in a pouch?
fact: Red kangaroos can leap more than 9 meters in a single bound.

q: How many legs does a spider have?
fact: Spiders have eight legs, while insects have only six.

q: Which animal is well known for being able to change its skin color?
fact: Chameleons change color by adjusting special pigment cells in their skin.

q: What is the largest flightless bird in the world?
fact: Ostriches lay the largest eggs of any living land animal.

q: Which insect produces honey?
fact: A single honey bee colony can contain up to 60,000 bees.

q: Which nocturnal bird is known for hooting and turning its head far around?
fact: Some owls can rotate their heads up to 270 degrees.

q: Which sea animal has eight arms and a soft body with no bones?
fact: Octopuses are considered among the most intelligent invertebrates.

q: Which domestic animal is known for purring when it is content?
fact: Cats can make over 100 different vocal sounds.

q: Which is the only mammal capable of true powered flight?
fact: There are more than 1,400 species of bats worldwide.

q: Which animal is the largest animal known to have ever lived?
fact: A blue whale's tongue alone can weigh as much as an elephant.

q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
fact: Two of an octopus's three hearts pump blood to its gills, and one pumps it to the body.

q: What color is a polar bear's skin underneath its white fur?
fact: Polar bear fur is not actually white, it is translucent and looks white because it reflects light.

q: Which bird is the fastest animal in the world when it dives?
fact: Peregrine falcons can dive at speeds over 240 mph.

q: Which mammal lays eggs instead of giving birth to live young?
fact: The platypus is one of only five living species of egg-laying mammals called monotremes.

q: What is a group of wolves called?
fact: Wolf packs are usually family groups led by a breeding pair.

q: Which animal has fingerprints that are very similar to human fingerprints?
fact: Koalas have unique fingerprints, just like humans.

q: What is a baby frog called?
fact: Tadpoles breathe through gills before they grow lungs and legs.

q: Which is the largest fish in the world?
fact: Whale sharks can grow longer than a city bus but eat mostly plankton.

q: Which bird is the only bird that can fly backwards?
fact: Hummingbirds can beat their wings up to 80 times per second.

q: In which animal does the male carry the babies in a special pouch?
fact: Male seahorses carry developing young in a brood pouch until they are born.

q: Which giant reptile is known for living well over 100 years?
fact: Some giant tortoises are believed to have lived for more than 150 years.

q: What do you call an animal that is active mainly at night?
fact: Owls, bats and many other nocturnal animals have special senses adapted for darkness.

q: Which amphibian can regenerate its limbs, heart and parts of its brain?
fact: Axolotls keep their larval features for their whole lives, a trait called neoteny.

q: Which is the only mammal in the world covered in scales?
fact: Pangolin scales are made of keratin, the same material as human fingernails.

q: Which tiny animal is famous for surviving the vacuum of space in experiments?
fact: Tardigrades, also called water bears, can survive extreme heat, cold and radiation.

q: A narwhal's long spiral tusk is actually what body part?
fact: A narwhal's tusk is usually its left canine tooth growing through its lip.

q: How many chambers does a cow's stomach have?
fact: A cow's four stomach chambers help it digest tough plant material like grass.

q: Which venomous primate is found in Southeast Asia?
fact: The slow loris is one of the very few venomous mammals in the world.

q: What makes the skin of a glass frog special?
a: It is translucent, so its organs can be seen from below
It is covered in tiny glass-like scales
fact: Glass frogs are mostly active at night and live in rainforests of Central and South America.
